definition: The total of the data values divided by how many values there are, written $\bar{x}$ ($\mu$ for a whole population).
For grouped data with equal class widths, the class with the highest frequency.

The square root of the variance, measuring how far data values typically lie from the mean; adding a constant to every value leaves it unchanged, and multiplying every value by $k$ multiplies it by $\lvert k\rvert$.
The mean of the squared distances of the data values from the mean, equal to the square of the standard deviation; for a data set it divides by $n$, the number of values.
